title: 3AGameFactory-Motion Beats Rigging Baselines on DivDynBench
summary: New framework pairs Claude Opus 5.5 with deterministic executor, scores 62.07 on DivDynBench versus 48.29 raw LLM baseline at $0.08 per task.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- 3AGameFactory-Motion pairs an LLM with a deterministic rigging and kinematics executor, scoring 62.07 on DivDynBench versus 48.29 for raw Claude.
- DivDynBench introduces 850 motion tasks across six morphology categories, testing long-horizon instructions with precise timing, angle and repetition requirements.
- The framework achieves 0.939 source fidelity on rigging tasks, outperforming Puppeteer, UniRig and RigAnything at roughly $0.08 per task.


Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, HKUST, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Tencent Hunyuan and Peking University officially released 3AGameFactory-Motion on November 24, 2026, a framework that pairs an LLM with a deterministic rigging and kinematics executor. Paired with Claude Opus 5.5, the system scored 62.07 overall on the new DivDynBench benchmark versus 48.29 for the raw Claude baseline, at roughly $0.08 per task. The paper introduces both the framework and the benchmark, addressing a longstanding gap in long-horizon motion synthesis for diverse character morphologies.


## Release Date and Availability


The research paper was officially released on November 24, 2026, and posted to public preprint servers the same day. The framework is currently available for academic evaluation, with DivDynBench assets and task specifications published alongside the paper. The authors report that production integration timelines remain under discussion with industry partners.


## How the Framework Works


3AGameFactory-Motion operates in two stages. First, the LLM emits compact parametric skeleton and motion programs that encode rigging logic, joint hierarchies and keyframe sequences. Second, a deterministic executor rigs the character, solves inverse kinematics constraints and refines the output to match source geometry and motion specifications. The separation of symbolic reasoning from numerical execution lets the pipeline handle complex multi-phase instructions such as "raise the left wing to 60 degrees within two seconds, flap three times, then glide and land" without halting or skipping phases.


On rigging fidelity, the framework reports a source-fidelity score of 0.939, ahead of Puppeteer at 0.714, UniRig at 0.449 and RigAnything at 0.449. Swapping Claude for a GPT-6.1 agent moves the overall score from 45.86 baseline to 61.06 with the executor, suggesting the gains ride on the rigging-and-solver scaffold rather than the model.


## DivDynBench: A New Yardstick for Motion Synthesis


DivDynBench covers 50 assets and 850 motion tasks across six morphology categories:


- Humanoid characters with standard bipedal skeletons
- Multiped creatures including quadrupeds and hexapods
- Axial bodies such as snakes and worms
- Winged entities with articulated flight surfaces
- Mixed-limb hybrids combining legs, wings and tails
- Mechanical rigs including robots and vehicles


The benchmark splits into 428 text cases and 422 numeric cases. Text cases specify natural-language motion descriptions, while numeric cases encode precise timing, angle, repetition and trajectory parameters. The task format is the point: prior systems rarely complete every phase in order or meet specified constraints, the authors write.


## Cost and Performance Comparison


At $0.08 per task, 3AGameFactory-Motion delivers a roughly 28 percent score improvement over the raw Claude Opus 5.5 baseline at one-third the cost of earlier hybrid approaches. The deterministic executor eliminates redundant sampling passes and geometric re-meshing, cutting per-task latency from 14.2 seconds to 3.7 seconds on average. The framework processes all six morphology categories with a single set of rigging templates, reducing engineering overhead for game studios and animation pipelines.


## What This Means


3AGameFactory-Motion demonstrates that pairing an LLM with a deterministic executor can outperform end-to-end neural approaches on structured motion tasks, while maintaining interpretability and cost discipline. The DivDynBench benchmark provides a reproducible testbed for future rigging and motion-synthesis research across diverse character types. For production teams, the framework offers a path to automate complex multi-phase animation workflows without sacrificing precision or geometric fidelity.
